subject: factor mean invariance with non-invariant intercepts

messages.author: 65310bd941552ff6
messages.subject: factor mean invariance with non-invariant intercepts
parts:
Hello,

I´m currently testing measurement Invariance across gender. In my two-factor model with ten items on item intercept was non-invariant and freed therefore. Now I want to test factor mean differences, but I´m not sure how to handle the factor with the invariant item.

in a paper I read the following statement:

 

"We used this partial strong MI model as the baseline model to conduct latent mean comparisons, keeping in mind that factor mean differences were now only based on the nine DT tests [inidactors] whose intercepts were fixed. An additional model was specified (Model SOI-pm) that was identical with Model SOI-p, except that latent means were fixed to be equal across groups. [...] It should be noted that the partial strong MI model used here is exploratory in character, and that mean differences on the tests [indicators] with free intercepts across groups are now unexplained by their respective factor." (p.4)

 

Kuhn, J. T., & Holling, H. (2009). Measurement Invariance of Divergent Thinking Across Gender, Age, and School Forms. European Journal of Psychological Assessment, 25(1), 1-7



Therefore I assumed that factor mean differences are only based on items with fixed intercepts, without any additional restriction of the model. But now someone told me that this is not true and therefore I´m confused.

Whats right? And do I have to delete this Item to test factor mean invariance or should  I refrain from testing this factor at all?


I´d be happy if someone could help with this problem.

Kathrin

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: factor mean invariance with non-invariant intercepts
parts:
Two items per factor with intercepts (and loadings) constrained to equality across groups can be sufficient to give meaning to differences in factor means (if they are the right two). Nine items per factor is more than enough. The item not constrained will not participate in defining the factor mean difference, but you do not need to discard the item, or the factor. The analysis is exploratory because you found the discrepant item with an ex post analysis, which raises the possibility of capitalizing on chance. But with 9 of 10 itme intercepts constrained to equality, I would wager that partial scalar invariance is well established. So carry on with the analysis, leaving the one item's intercept not constrained.
--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: factor mean invariance with non-invariant intercepts
parts: "The item not constrained will not participate in defining the factor mean difference" can you explain why?

Latent variables are not observed, so we can only infer their distributional properties (means, variances) indirectly via their hypothesized effects on indicators.  We typically fix latent means for identification, but we can release those identification constraints (except for one group/occasion) when we constrain loadings and intercepts across groups/occasions.  When you constrain 5 out of 6 intercepts to equality, the differences in observed means of those 5 indicators between groups are assumed to be due only to differences in the common-factor means between groups. Because the 6th intercept is not constrained across groups, the observed means of the 6th indicator can differ not only because of common-factor mean differences, but also differences in the measurement parameters (intercepts). 

This is a general SEM question, not specific to lavaan, so SEMNET would be a more appropriate forum to post this question.

www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
